from __future__ import annotations

import collections
import threading
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from streamlit.runtime.scriptrunner_utils.thread_safe_set import ThreadSafeSet

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from streamlit.proto.PageProfile_pb2 import Command


class SharedRunState:
    """Container for the mutable per-run state shared across threads within a
    single script run.

    A single script run may spawn helper threads (e.g. parallel fragment
    workers) that all read from and write to the same tracking sets and command
    telemetry. Bundling that state here — instead of spreading bare fields
    across ``ScriptRunContext`` — keeps the mutation surface small and lets the
    telemetry counters be updated atomically from multiple threads.

    The widget/form/fragment sets are ``ThreadSafeSet`` instances that guard
    their own access. The command telemetry (the tracked-command list and the
    per-command counter) is guarded by a dedicated lock so that concurrent
    ``track_command`` calls never lose a command.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.widget_ids_this_run: ThreadSafeSet[str] = ThreadSafeSet()
        self.widget_user_keys_this_run: ThreadSafeSet[str] = ThreadSafeSet()
        self.form_ids_this_run: ThreadSafeSet[str] = ThreadSafeSet()
        self.new_fragment_ids: ThreadSafeSet[str] = ThreadSafeSet()

        # Telemetry state is guarded by its own lock because ``track_command``
        # performs a read-modify-write across both the list and the counter.
        self._telemetry_lock = threading.Lock()
        self._tracked_commands: list[Command] = []
        self._tracked_commands_counter: collections.Counter[str] = (
            collections.Counter()
        )

    @property
    def tracked_commands(self) -> tuple[Command, ...]:
        """An immutable snapshot of the commands tracked so far this run.

        Returns a ``tuple`` (never the underlying list) so downstream consumers
        cannot mutate the tracked commands out from under the run.
        """
        with self._telemetry_lock:
            return tuple(self._tracked_commands)

    @property
    def tracked_commands_count(self) -> int:
        """The number of commands currently stored in the tracked list.

        This is capped by the per-command maximum enforced in ``track_command``
        and so may be smaller than the raw counts returned by
        ``command_count_for``.
        """
        with self._telemetry_lock:
            return len(self._tracked_commands)

    def track_command(self, command: Command, max_per_command: int) -> None:
        """Record a command in the telemetry state.

        The command is appended to the tracked list only if a command with the
        same name has been tracked fewer than ``max_per_command`` times so far.
        The raw per-name counter is always incremented, regardless of the cap,
        so ``command_count_for`` reflects the true number of invocations.

        Thread-safe: concurrent calls hold the telemetry lock, so no command is
        lost even when helper threads track commands simultaneously.
        """
        with self._telemetry_lock:
            if self._tracked_commands_counter[command.name] < max_per_command:
                self._tracked_commands.append(command)
            self._tracked_commands_counter.update([command.name])

    def command_count_for(self, name: str) -> int:
        """Return the raw, uncapped number of times ``name`` has been tracked."""
        with self._telemetry_lock:
            return self._tracked_commands_counter[name]

    def reset(self) -> None:

## New module: `shared_run_state.py`

Created `lib/streamlit/runtime/scriptrunner_utils/shared_run_state.py` exporting `SharedRunState`, which bundles all mutable per-run state:

- **`tracked_commands`** property → returns an immutable `tuple` (so `.append()` raises `AttributeError`); `()` when empty.
- **`tracked_commands_count`** → int length of the (capped) tracked list.
- **`track_command(command, max_per_command)`** → appends only if that name has been tracked fewer than `max_per_command` times, but *always* bumps the raw per-name counter. Guarded by a dedicated telemetry lock so concurrent threads never lose a command.
- **`command_count_for(name)`** → the raw, uncapped per-name count.
